text.p: Dutch construction group Koninklijke Volker Stevin NV said on Wednesday it had won a 400 million guilder ($236 million) order from the Dutch state as part of a major infrastructural project to re-develop a Hague suburb.

"The total project will be worth several hundred million guilders...and will mean a major improvement in our order portfolio in the coming years," Volker Stevin finance director Pim Dijkman told a news conference on first-half results.

The project, costing a total of 450 million guilders, involves the building of a tunnel complex and the construction of 700 housing units around the A-14 motorway through The Hague suburb of Voorburg, the transport ministry said.
Building is due to start in 1998, with the final houses due for delivery in 2002, the ministry said.

Volker Stevin shares, trading modestly higher on pre-bourse news of a 15 percent increase in net profit from normal operations to 12 million guilders, leaped to a new year-high of 144.90 guilders after the order was announced.
The shares later closed the session up 3.70 guilders at 143.00 guilders.
"This innovative project breaks new ground in tackling problems of space shortages," the ministry said in a statement.
"It's a dream contract for Volker Stevin, making optimal use of its two core competencies -- housing and road-building," ING Barings analyst Paul Verbraeken said.

"I had already upgraded the stock to a 'buy' on the basis of the first-half results -- this is really the cherry on the cake," he added in an initial reaction ahead of an analysts' briefing on Thursday.
Verbraeken said that as chief contractor Volker Stevin would likely earn more than the going rate on the project.
"Of course there will be an additional extra in return for the risk they are taking on," he said, adding "but obviously the firm is well-experienced in assessing such risks -- they do it every day."

Volker Stevin earlier reported net profit in the first half jumped to 16.1 million guilders, boosted by a 4.1 million guilder book profit on the sale of a stake in its Ecotech environmental services unit. ($1=1.696 Guilder)
